cultural.vision_reason: This is a carved wooden bark shredder with classic Northwest Coast formline design (crest figure flanked by wolves/bears), a tool type and art style consistent with Tlingit material culture.

physical.title: shredder
physical.summary: Bark shredder made of wood and decorated with a central figure, possibly a hawk or eagle with a human face: the face and limbs are carved while the wings are painted on to the board. The central figure is flanked by two crouching wolves (or possibly bears) with protruding tounges. The front of the board is painted in red and black pigments, red for the central figure's feathers, tail, mouth and hood and the wolves' bodies, noses and tounges. and black for the wolves' heads and the central figures arms, face and body. The reverse is largely undecorated except for the wolves, which are painted as on the front side and two vertical strips of red that descent from the wolves elbows to the base of the board. The back shows some adze marks indicating that it is likely to be of native construction.
